back: A person who freely offers time, skills or labour for others without expecting payment.
Work done freely and without payment to meet a community need or help people in need.
Clean-ups, helping the elderly and sick, tree planting, community gardens, school projects (also disaster relief, borehole repair, tutoring).

front: Name two traditional forms of communal voluntary work.
back: The work party (nhimbe/ilima) and the chief's field (zunde ramambo).

front: Give two rural and two urban community needs.
back: Rural: broken boreholes, soil erosion. Urban: blocked drains and litter, youth unemployment and crime.

front: How does volunteering benefit the volunteer?
back: Skills and experience, satisfaction and confidence, friendships and networks, respect and references.

front: How does volunteering benefit the community?
back: Meets needs quickly, saves money, builds unity, supports the vulnerable, protects the environment, encourages self-reliance.
Lack of time, lack of materials and transport, loss of interest, poor planning.
